first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing creates pressure toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 explicitly records that it materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized — matching acquisition pressure with a tactic known to erode retention would trade long-term qualified revenue for short-term volume, so it is excluded despite being the most topically 'responsive' option. The two metrics actually declining are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%). Of the candidates addressing those, activation_messaging (memory_91) targets the larger decline and carries no recorded downside, while simplify_onboarding is constrained by memory_86's segment caveat (raises early churn in complex-workspace accounts). Referral incentives and enterprise sales-assist address neither declining metric this week. On verification: I deliberately spend the budget on memory_91 and memory_31 rather than on memories that already carry caveats. memory_86 and memory_73 retained explicit 'however' clauses through consolidation, which shows caveats do survive summarization here — so re-pulling them buys little. memory_91 and memory_31 are stated as unqualified wins, and an unqualified win is exactly the shape a summary takes when a segment-specific limitation was dropped. memory_91 is the record I intend to act on, and memory_31 is the closest adjacent claim (signup/activation lift) that could either reinforce or complicate it. I am treating both as provisional until the archive returns. Contingency: if memory_91's source record reveals a segment where activation messaging suppressed retention or first-value quality, I will narrow the experiment to the unaffected segments rather than proceed at full scope; if it reveals the effect was measured only on week-one engagement with no downstream revenue linkage, I will treat the lift as a proxy and instrument for qualified-pipeline effect, not just engagement. Running at standard_experiment scale rather than broad rollout because the supporting evidence is a day-61 summary I have not yet confirmed, and because engagement lift is not the same as sustainable qualified revenue — I will hold retention and complex-workspace churn as explicit guardrail metrics given the pattern memory_86 and memory_73 establish, where adoption gains masked retention costs.

final.rationale:
The archive confirmed memory_91 with no hidden segment caveat: activation messaging delivered +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, and 30-day retention slightly positive at +1%. That is the rare case where the adoption lift did not come at a retention cost, which is precisely the failure mode memory_73 and memory_86 warn about. It also targets the largest live decline (activation -6% QoQ), and the effect size (+6% activation) is roughly the magnitude needed to recover the quarter's loss. Proceeding with activation_messaging.

On the alternatives: promotional_pricing remains excluded despite being the most topically responsive answer to the competitor's entry pricing — memory_73 records that it materially reduced 30-day retention, and buying price-sensitive SMB volume with a tactic known to erode retention converts the primary objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) into short-term volume. Losing some price-sensitive accounts to a competitor is a smaller loss than acquiring churning ones. simplify_onboarding is now the strongest runner-up: exp_31 is the only candidate with a directly measured qualified revenue outcome (+4%), which is the actual objective, and onboarding completion is genuinely down 4%. I am not choosing it because exp_31 explicitly did not replicate outside SMB, memory_86 records elevated early churn in complex-workspace accounts, and its retention read was -1% rather than positive. Against a competitor already pulling price-sensitive SMB, an SMB-only intervention with a mild retention drag is the weaker bet this week. referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist address neither declining metric.

Remaining uncertainty I am not resolving away: exp_91 measured engagement, activation, and retention, but never qualified revenue. Activation is a proxy, and the objective is qualified revenue — exp_31 shows the two can move together, but that link is assumed here, not demonstrated. I am also carrying forward that exp_91's segment breakdown is unknown; the record showed no caveat, but absence of a reported caveat is weaker evidence than a reported null. Holding at standard_experiment rather than broad rollout for those two reasons, with instrumentation on qualified pipeline (not just engagement) and guardrails on 30-day retention and complex-workspace churn, segmented so a pooled positive cannot conceal a segment that is being harmed. If qualified revenue fails to track the activation lift, the result should be read as a proxy win rather than an objective win, and simplify_onboarding scoped to SMB becomes the next slot's candidate.
